title: Hardik Pandya Sports Tonsured Head During Tirumala Temple Visit with Girlfriend Mahieka Sharma
excerpt: The Indian cricket star was photographed with a shaved head alongside his model girlfriend at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple, sparking fresh discussion about the couple's deepening spiritual bond.
body:
• Hardik Pandya visited the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala with girlfriend Mahieka Sharma, sporting a freshly tonsured head as part of the traditional ritual offering.
  • The tonsure ritual at Tirumala is a centuries-old Hindu devotional practice symbolizing surrender, gratitude, and spiritual renewal before Lord Venkateswara.
  • The visit follows a series of public spiritual outings by the couple, including temple visits during the T20 World Cup 2026 and private pujas at home.
  • The temple trip has intensified speculation about their relationship, which Pandya made Instagram official in October 2025 after his divorce from Natasa Stankovic.

Pandya's Pilgrimage to Tirumala

Indian cricket all-rounder Hardik Pandya turned heads for reasons beyond his batting when he was spotted at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirumala with a completely shaved head. The 32-year-old was accompanied by girlfriend Mahieka Sharma, and photos from the visit quickly spread across social media.

Pandya's tonsured look marked a departure from his signature styled hair. The cricketer, long known for bold hairstyle choices ranging from platinum blonde to electric blue, appeared to have undergone the traditional head-shaving ritual at the temple's Kalyanakatta tonsure halls, according to reports in Gulf News and NDTV Sports.

A Sacred Tradition at India's Richest Temple

The tonsure ritual at Tirumala is one of Hinduism's most recognizable devotional acts. Millions of pilgrims each year offer their hair at the hilltop shrine of Lord Venkateswara as a sign of surrender, gratitude, or fulfillment of a vow known as mokku. According to temple mythology, a devotee once accidentally injured Lord Venkateswara's head, prompting Goddess Neela Devi to offer a portion of her own hair. The deity then declared that devotees who offered their hair would receive divine blessings.

The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD), which administers the temple, collects and auctions the donated hair. Revenue generated supports free meal programs, temple maintenance, education initiatives, and charitable works across Andhra Pradesh.

"This is about faith, not fashion. When someone like Hardik Pandya goes through the tonsure, it shows devotion transcends celebrity status."

— A temple official, speaking to Moneycontrol

A Couple's Spiritual Journey

The Tirumala visit is the latest in a string of spiritual outings for Pandya and Sharma. In March, the couple visited Mumbai's Siddhivinayak Temple hours before India's T20 World Cup semifinal against England at the Wankhede Stadium. That visit, where they were photographed sharing a shawl during the rituals, went viral. Mahieka also visited Siddhivinayak solo before the IPL 2026 season, wearing Mumbai Indians colors as she prayed for Pandya's franchise.

Late last year, Pandya shared videos of a traditional hawan ceremony at his home with Mahieka seated beside him, both dressed in matching ethnic wear. The post, captioned "My big 3" — referring to cricket, son Agastya, and Mahieka — drew widespread praise from fans for showing the cricketer's grounded, spiritual side.

Relationship in the Spotlight

Pandya made his relationship with Mahieka Sharma, an award-winning model and yoga trainer who has appeared in campaigns for Tanishq, Vivo, and Uniqlo, Instagram official in October 2025. The announcement came more than a year after his divorce from Serbian model Natasa Stankovic in 2024. The couple shares a son, Agastya.

Since going public, Pandya and Sharma's relationship has attracted constant media scrutiny. A viral photo showing Mahieka wearing what appeared to be sindoor sparked wedding rumors in June, though neither party confirmed the speculation. Earlier, a diamond ring spotted on Mahieka's finger led to engagement chatter, which she dismissed, calling it simply "nice jewellery."

"I understand that living in the public eye comes with attention and scrutiny, it's part of the life I've chosen. But... women deserve dignity. Everyone deserves boundaries."

— Hardik Pandya, in an Instagram story addressing paparazzi behavior

The Diaspora Connection

For the global Indian community, Pandya's public embrace of Hindu rituals resonates as a visible affirmation of cultural traditions. The tonsure at Tirumala, one of India's most visited pilgrimage sites drawing over 60,000 devotees daily, remains a practice that bridges generations and geographies for diaspora families maintaining spiritual ties to India.

What's Next

Pandya, who was part of India's T20 World Cup 2026 campaign and the IPL season, is expected to feature in upcoming international assignments. Whether the tonsured look signals a personal vow fulfilled or a new beginning for the couple remains their private matter — but the images from Tirumala have already become one of the most talked-about cricket-adjacent moments of the year.
